slot.brief: Use limiting molar conductivities of two known strong electrolytes to compute Λ°m of a third (e.g., acetic acid from HCl, NaCl, CH3COONa).

stem: Given $\Lambda_m^\circ$ values of $\text{HCl}$, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ as $426$, $126$ and $91$ $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, respectively, calculate $\Lambda_m^\circ$ of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

verdicts.working: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426 + 91 − 126 = 391 S cm² mol⁻¹.
